newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks lose early gains to end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks lose early gains to end mixed.

text.p: Toronto's stock market lost early gains to close mixed on Wednesday as early euphoria over surprisingly low U.S. producer prices for April subsided.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index dipped 1.06 points to finish at 6248.18. Total volume was 108.7 million shares worth C$1.64 billion ($1.18 billion).
The U.S. producer price index dipped 0.6 percent in April compared to economists' forecasts for a flat month. The soft data calmed fears of a U.S. interest rate hike.
But investors remained wary as the Toronto market neared its all-time high of 6348.02 points set on March 11.
"Despite the producer prices looking good ... we're still at all-time highs," said Pier Donnini, head trader of instititutional equities at brokerage Yorkton Securities.
Investors are waiting for more U.S. economic data on Thursday, including April's consumer price index.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices ended lower, led by golds, consumer products and base metals. The gainers included oils and utilities.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 526 to 462, while 298 issues closed flat.
In individual stocks, Gandalf Technologies Inc. tumbled 1.04 to 2.44 in heavy trading of 2.7 million shares after Tuesday's gain of almost 150 percent.
After the market closed, the computer networking company reported a fourth-quarter loss of US$0.43 a share for the period ended March 31 versus a break-even quarter last year.
Dreco Energy Services Ltd. jumped 12 to 65 after news that the company would merge with National-Oilwell Inc.
Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd. slipped 0.55 to 28 after announcing that Chief Executive David Hentschel would be replaced by Chief Financial Officer Victor Zaleschuk.
